title: Beef and Noodles
subtitle: A Midwestern American braised beef and egg noodle dish
excerpt: Slow-braised beef chuck pulled into chunks and served over thick egg noodles in a rich, reduced stock. A filling, budget-friendly midwestern classic.
sourceNotes: Midwestern American comfort food. Beef chuck is braised in stock until very tender, then the braising liquid is reduced and thickened to coat the noodles.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the beef and braising liquid without the noodles. Cook fresh noodles when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Beef braises well in large batches. Freeze the braised beef in the reduced liquid.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the beef a day ahead and refrigerate. Skim any fat from the surface before reheating. Cook noodles fresh.

content.text: Beef and noodles is a simple braise: the beef cooks low and slow in stock until it falls apart, then the liquid is thickened and poured over egg noodles. The long cooking time does the work for you.
Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the dutch oven over high heat. Brown the beef in two batches until deep brown on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the butter and onion. Cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Scatter the flour over the onion and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the stock gradually, scraping up any brown bits from the base of the pot.
Return the beef to the pot. Add the Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves, and thyme. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 90 minutes until the beef is very tender and breaks apart easily with a spoon.
Remove the beef and break it into large chunks. Discard the bay leaves. Boil the liquid uncovered for 10 minutes to reduce and thicken slightly.
Cook the egg noodles in salted water until tender. Drain and return to the pan. Return the beef to the sauce, stir, and serve over the noodles.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 90 minutes.
items.cause: The simmer was too vigorous and dried out the braising liquid, or the pieces were too large.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low. Add a splash more stock and cook for another 20 to 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The flour did not cook long enough, or the liquid was not reduced at the end.
items.fix: Boil uncovered for longer. Stir a tablespoon of cornflour mixed with cold water into the simmering sauce.

items.cause: They sat undrained for too long.
items.fix: Toss drained noodles immediately with a small knob of butter to stop them clumping.
